title: Judiciary's P84.1-billion proposed budget breezes through Senate
summary: The Senate on Friday quickly approved the P84.1-billion proposed budget of the Judicial branch without any questions asked.

blocks.text: The Senate on Friday quickly approved the P84.1-billion proposed budget of the Judicial branch without any questions asked.

Senator Francis Pangilinan, the budget sponsor in the Upper Chamber, presented the proposed funding of the Supreme Court (SC) and lower courts, Court of Appeals (CA), the Sandiganbayan, the Court of Tax Appeals, and the Presidential Electoral Tribunal.

"Pondohan natin nang buo ang budget na ito. Igalang natin ang fiscal autonomy ng Hudikatura at bigyan natin ang sambayanan ng isang sistemang pangkatarungang nararapat sa tiwala nating lahat," Pangilinan said in his opening statement.
(Let us fully fund this budget. Let us respect the Judiciary's fiscal autonomy and give the country a system that is just and worthy of our trust.)
Pangilinan said 98,633 cases were pending for five years in first- and second-level courts as of August 2026, while 49,475 have been pending for 10 years.

The court has taken steps to address this backlog, with the Revised Guidelines for Continuous Trial of Criminal Cases mandating that trying cases under regular cases should not surpass 180 days from the first trial date.

The SC has a P71.702-billion budget, the CA has P7.414 billion, the Sandiganbayan has P3.517 billion, the Court of Tax Appeals has P1.320 billion, and the Presidential Electoral Tribunal has P179.78 billion.
This is the first judiciary budget under the newly installed SC Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda, who assumed his position earlier in November.
With no senator lining up to question the budget, Senator Risa Hontiveros moved to have the Judiciary budget deemed submitted.

"Mister President, there being no reservations for interpellation, I move to close the period of interpellation of the budget of the judiciary, including the Supreme Court of the Philippines and the lower courts, Presidential Electoral Tribunal, Sandiganbayan, the Court of Appeals and the Court of Tax Appeals and that the same be deemed submitted for the body's consideration," Hontiveros said.

"Is there any objection? Hearing none, the period of interpellation for the budget of the Supreme Court and all of its offices is hereby closed and deemed submitted," Senate President Win Gatchalian said. — VDV, GMA News
